The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, has pledged to unite Nigeria, tackle insecurity and fight corruption if elected president in the 2027 general election. He promised to pursue kidnappers to their hideouts. Obi disclosed this on Wednesday during a town hall meeting in Calabar, Cross River State with party stakeholders and supporters. He stressed that his administration would prioritise national unity, security, education, healthcare and the welfare of citizens. He said, “Nigeria is currently divided. We will work to unite this country, because uniting this nation would provide the strength needed to confront insecurity and other national challenges. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources “Our commitment is to unite Nigeria. Nigeria today is not united. If we unite Nigeria today, we will have the strength to fight insecurity.” The presidential candidate said his administration would not tolerate the prevailing security challenges, particularly kidnapping and attacks on schoolchildren. “Anybody that kidnaps school children and goes into the bush, we will be in that bush with him, wherever it is. We are not scared of him,” Obi said. He said security agencies under his watch would pursue kidnappers into their hideouts to ensure the safe rescue of abducted schoolchildren. 2027: Obasanjo’s son backs Tinubu’s re-election Evening recap: Free NIN slips, Yamal’s UCL record, other top stories Soldiers rescue nine kidnap victims in Kebbi, recover 108 livestock On corruption, he promised to confront the menace decisively, insisting that public funds must be deployed for the benefit and welfare of Nigerians. He said his administration would pursue corruption with determination to discourage the diversion of public resources for personal gain. “We will fight corruption head-on. We want people to stop stealing public money. Public money must be used for public good and for the welfare of the people,” he said. Obi also pledged increased investment in education and healthcare, describing both sectors as critical areas of national development. He said his political partnership represented a new approach to governance, anchored on shared responsibility and a commitment to transforming the country. “We represent a new Nigeria that is possible. We represent a governance that people have not seen in Nigeria before,” he said. The former Anambra governor said the engagement in Cross River was organised to provide residents with an opportunity to ask questions and express their concerns without restrictions. He urged participants to make comments and seek clarification freely, saying the purpose of the meeting was to listen to the people. “The style is to listen to you. You are free to ask any question. No restriction. Make any comment. That is why we are here,” he said. Emem Julius
